Puis, on a croqué trois fois dans la pomme.
Enfin, il ne reste que le trognon.
D'abord, la banane n'est pas épluchée.
Ensuite, un morceau de peau pend sur le côté.
Puis, trois morceaux de peau pendent.
Enfin, il ne reste que la peau vide.
D'abord, il y a deux tranches de pain.
Ensuite, une tranche est couverte de confiture.
Puis, le sandwich est coupé en deux.
Enfin, il ne reste que la croûte et des miettes.
D'abord, le gâteau est entier.
Ensuite, on a coupé une part.
Puis, la moitié du gâteau a disparu.
Enfin, il ne reste que des miettes.
D'abord, la barrière est toute blanche.
Ensuite, deux planches sont peintes.
Puis, quatre planches sont peintes.
Enfin, toute la barrière est peinte.
D'abord, la carte est blanche.
Ensuite, on dessine une fleur sur la carte.
Puis, on écrit trois lignes.
Enfin, la carte est dans une enveloppe avec un timbre.
D'abord, il y a une feuille de papier.
Ensuite, la feuille est découpée en cinq bandes.
Puis, deux bandes sont collées en anneaux.
Enfin, les cinq anneaux forment une guirlande.
D'abord, il n'y a aucune trace de pas dans le sable.
Ensuite, un enfant marche et laisse trois traces de pas.
Puis, l'enfant trouve un coquillage.
Enfin, l'enfant revient sur sa serviette avec le coquillage.

enAudit: CURSIVE RULING (fr): ship fr-trad, refuse fr-moderne. Rendered side by side (a-z, A-Z, words): fr-trad is the MEN/Eduscol 2013 school model French children learn today - upright, loops on b f h k l and on the e, looped descenders f g j y z, the French r, s, x (two c) and looped z, open p, and CURSIVE capitals (L, H, C read as the cahier models). fr-moderne is not a French school hand: no ascender loops, it lifts after f g q j, and its capitals are PRINT capitals (a Majuscules cursives face in fr-moderne would print block letters). One honest limitation of fr-trad, not a refusal: the ISOLATED model letter in the margin cell has no delie d attaque (entry stroke from the baseline) that French pupils are taught; the grey chains show the joined form, so the page stays usable - the landing should not claim the model letter shows the start of the stroke.

CURSIVE LEVELS (code vs French paper): the design table puts capitals and copy at CE1 on Seyes 3 mm, but G2-377 refuses them (X 11.34 < the G2 floor 14). Real CE1 Seyes is 2-3 mm, so the floor can never pass at CE1. fr therefore ships Majuscules cursives and Copier une phrase at level cp (Seyes 4 mm, a genuine CP use: writing one s prenom with its capital and copying short sentences are CP objectives). If CE1 landings are wanted, the floor or the seyesI table must change - a code decision, not data.

habitats adapt claims use It / Its: in any gendered language a pronoun leaks or contradicts the answer (fish-gills is answered by the ray = la raie, whale-blowhole by the whale = la baleine; il respire would exclude them). fr uses Cet animal ... for the multi-answer claims and a pronoun only where exactly one masculine animal is trueOf. Every Romance and Germanic panel should check this.

habitats birds 2/heron is drawn as a WHITE STORK (white body, black wings, orange bill, red legs): a French child says cigogne, and storks feed in meadows and fields as much as in ponds, so on a page with Mare AND Prairie the heron has two defensible answers. Added cigogne to names.heron for the leak check; the claim table (lives:[pond]) needs a human decision (exclude the picture, or bar it from pages with a meadow window).

cursive animals/cat and animals/tiger are both drawn as orange striped kittens (the tiger is a cub with a cat face): on one F3/F4 page chat and tigre match either picture. fr drops animals/tiger from its words (25 words, still >= 12); the pinned list needs a lookalike rule for every locale.

sink-or-float F2 (G2-382): the clay BOAT is drawn as a hollow bowl - a French child says un bol - the exact ambiguity the design cites for rejecting A s bowl form; and the transfer card bolt is drawn BRASS-yellow, so the steel bolt vs steel ship (same material) premise is not visible on the page. Neither breaks the answer, both weaken the teaching point.

Instructions that are more than one sentence in EN (the brief asks for one child-level sentence): habitats G1-398 (2), habitats G2-381 report (3), cursive G2-386 words (2), cursive G3-401 copy (2). fr writes each as one sentence.

Pronoun instructions without an antecedent in EN: healthy-habits brushing Circle the word that tells when it happens (it = each picture; fr says Pour chaque image, entoure le mot qui dit quand cela se passe) and sink-or-float base ... a ring in the second tank after it (it = the test or the tank?).

story-sequencing F1: nothing on the page pairs cut strip k with story line k except order (already recorded by the faces doc); fr says colle-les sur leur corde to name the line as the drawn washing-line, but a visual cue (matching strip / cord colour or a small emblem) is still missing for pre-readers.

healthy-habits F5 chart: labels are greedy-wrapped, so se laver les mains breaks as se laver les / mains (article stranded at the line end). Acceptable, but a label with a forced break point (two literals per label) would read better in every Romance locale.

Health strand: no Health row exists yet in strand-names.ts, so apply-b6-locale.js will skip strandNames.Health with a warning; fr literal proposed Questionner le monde : la sante. Reading: Literature fr proposed Lecture : comprendre des recits.

Reconciliation round: the sandwich crust panel, the verify-vs-French-typography bug and the adapt pronoun/place leaks are fixed upstream; fr sandwich sentence 4 now names the finished crust (croûte), G3-400 fr verify() is clean.
